mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-22.7 to -16.4), indicating sustained recovery momentum in discretionary mobility that should continue to lift retail footfall over the next four weeks via persistence of the existing trend.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite three prior weeks of consecutive increase.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -20.0 to -14.3 over the snapshot window, reflecting resumed commuting that generates incidental weekday retail and dining visits, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following continued WORKPLACES improvement of more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility stalls or reverses (week-on-week change turns negative or falls below -17), reduced willingness to use shared transport will constrain access to retail districts, causing RETAIL_REC to flatten or decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change turns negative or TRANSIT falls below -17
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved each week from -24.1 to -15.7 but rate of improvement slowed from +3.8 to +0.9 points last week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT reversing or stalling below -17.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.4 to 3.7 while PARKS rose from -9.3 to 4.7 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than growth predicted by RESIDENTIAL alone, indicating no amplification from joint PARKS-RESIDENTIAL movement.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surged sharply from -9.3 to 8.4 between t-3w and t-1w then softened to 4.7 at t-0w, consistent with a seasonal outdoor-activity peak; as this seasonal pull fades, substitution away from parks back toward indoor retail and recreation venues will push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change turns negative after prior peak
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -9.3 to 8.4 then declined to 4.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even as PARKS continues to decline from its t-1w peak.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility suddenly drops more than 10 points week-on-week, this signals a renewed tightening of restrictions on business operations, which would simultaneously suppress retail footfall, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES currently improving steadily from -20.0 to -14.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 28 days despite a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 10 points in a single week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near +9 to +10 after rising from 5.4, suggesting baseline essential-trip demand has saturated; this ceiling effect implies no further incremental signal from essential mobility for predicting RETAIL_REC, so RETAIL_REC movement over the next week will be driven primarily by its own recent momentum rather than GROCERY_PHARM.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change falls below 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM change slowed from +2.3 (t-3w to t-2w) to -0.9 (t-1w to t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to track its own prior-week direction (rises last week but falls this week) once GROCERY_PHARM plateaus.
